subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call threshold data through workspace/internal hooks, or keep these lifecycle seams plugin-only except for a narrow observation event?
rationale: The missing surface is source-proven, but payload minimization, hook authority, event ordering, and threshold configuration are public API and security-boundary choices that automation should not choose.

options.title: Observation-Only Workspace Events
options.body: Add narrow workspace/internal lifecycle events with minimized metadata while leaving mutation, mid-turn control, and sensitive tool/session access in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Keep Lifecycle Plugin-Only
options.body: Treat existing `agent_end`, `before_tool_call`, `after_tool_call`, and `subagent_ended` plugin hooks as the supported lifecycle surface and decline workspace hook expansion for this data.

options.title: Design Unified Lifecycle Contract First
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one lifecycle model covering internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, payloads, thresholds, permissions, and ordering.

recommendation.title: Observation-Only Workspace Events
recommendation.body: Add narrow workspace/internal lifecycle events with minimized metadata while leaving mutation, mid-turn control, and sensitive tool/session access in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sits on hook contract, plugin API, and lifecycle/security boundaries where current history points most strongly to this owner.
